author: Swinhoe, 1860
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수천 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록
summary: 봄과 가을에 우리나라를 지나는 무리가 대부분인 나그네새이며, 한반도 전역의 갈밭에서 드물게 번식하는 여름새이기도 하다. 고원, 물가, 건조한 초지에 둥지를 틀고 6~8월 상순에 한배에 보통 4~6개의 알을 낳는다. 홀로 또는 암수가 함께 지내지만 번식지에서는 대개 빽빽하게 모여 살며, 먹이는 개개비와 비슷하다. 한국, 구북구 동부, 몽골, 만주, 아무르, 우수리, 사할린, 일본, 중국 등지에서 번식하고 중국 남부, 태국, 미얀마, 인도 아삼 지방에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Black-browed Reed Warbler (Acrocephalus bistrigiceps), adult in spring (sexes alike): forehead, crown, nape and back plain olive-tinged rusty-brown, unstreaked; a broad buffy-white supercilium bordered above by a bold blackish-brown stripe along each side of the crown; a dark brown eye-stripe below it; chin, centre of the throat and centre of the belly buffy-white; sides of the throat, breast, flanks and undertail coverts buff, deepest on the flanks; rump and uppertail coverts paler rusty-brown; wings and rounded tail plain brown; bill dark above, pale pinkish below; brown eye; greyish legs with a pinkish tinge.
art.pose: clinging to a reed stem, side view
art.scene: Korean reedbed beside water during spring migration; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view clinging upright to a reed stem: plain rusty-brown upperparts, buffy-white supercilium with a blackish crown-side stripe above it, buffy-white throat, buff breast and flanks, rounded tail, greyish-pink legs
adult, head in profile: bold blackish-brown stripe along the side of the crown above the buffy-white supercilium, dark eye-stripe, buffy-white chin and throat
art.build: Small reed warbler, about 14cm — about sparrow length but slimmer, and much smaller than an Oriental Reed Warbler. Flat crown and a straight, pointed bill shorter than the head. Legs greyish with a pinkish tinge, strong for clinging to vertical stems. Wings fairly short; at rest the wingtips reach only a little past the base of the tail. Tail medium-length and rounded. Clings upright to reed stems, often straddling two, and sings from a reed top.
avoid: Do not omit the blackish stripe above the pale supercilium; it is the species' key mark.
Do not paint streaks on the back (Locustella warblers).
Do not make it large and heavy-billed like Oriental Reed Warbler (Acrocephalus orientalis).
